newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria needs 2nd revision of '96 budget -speaker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria needs 2nd revision of '96 budget -speaker.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament will have to approve a second revision of this year's budget because revised annual targets have already been overshot, parliament speaker Blagovest Sendov said on Tuesday.
"Parliament will have to revise this year's budget as the budget deficit has overshot the planned target by more than 10 percent," state radio quoted Sendov as telling parliament.
Bulgaria's central government budget deficit topped the 1996 annual target by 21.1 percent on November 17 when it rose to 97.7 billion levs, Finance Ministry figures showed.
The budget is adopted by law and must therefore, be revised to legalise surplus expenditure.

Bulgaria already revised the budget once in July to meet high foreign and domestic debt payments and keep structural reform on track, raising the deficit target from 58.3 billion levs to 80.7 billion levs, or 4.9 percent of gross domestic product.
The rise in the deficit was mainly due to large interest payments on domestic debt, the ministry said.

The Bulgarian National Bank's central interest rate is currently set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually. The rate was increased to an all-time high of 300 percent two months ago to support the lev.
Cumulative inflation for the first 10 months hit 195 percent.
Government debt rose to 668.3 billion levs at the end of October from 640.6 billion levs a month earlier and 345.4 billion levs at the end of last year.
